comparisonNote: One shared brief. Identical starting files. Astra at medium effort in both harnesses. These are the files each delivered.
sharedBrief:
Make me a beautiful, complete falling-block puzzle game in one self-contained HTML file called arcade.html.

Make it feel like a little arcade game someone would actually want to keep. Choose a memorable name and visual style. Be creative: add thoughtful touches and delightful extras where they improve the experience.

It needs a real playable board, falling pieces that move and rotate, line clearing, scoring, a next-piece preview, hold, pause/resume, restart, and a game-over state. Include clear keyboard controls and touch controls that work on a phone. Make the interface comfortable on a small screen and attractive on a desktop. Sound is optional; if you add it, include a mute control.

Everything must work offline from this single file: no downloads, build step, external assets, or third-party dependencies. Use inline CSS and classic inline JavaScript. Keep the supplied package.json and test/delivery.test.js unchanged. Those starter tests check delivery packaging only. Add your own meaningful checks, inspect your work, and fix what you find before you finish.
conditions: Fresh BANTAM FACTORY build against the saved, completed native Astra baseline. Same creative brief and starting files; GPT-6 Astra at medium effort. The native baseline was recorded on September 8 in 404.9 seconds; this factory run on September 9 in 356.6 seconds, using commit 5d65012. The runs used maximum windows of ten and thirty minutes respectively and both finished naturally. The earlier native run overlapped other local work. Thirteen factory tests and ten native tests pass; both unedited games pass independent browser playtests. All eight factory usage receipts reconcile with the retained native provider trace. Previous builds remain privately archived.
usageNote: Recorded input, output, prefix-cache tokens and wall clock. Prefix-cache tokens are included in total input. Output includes reported reasoning. All requests in these two completed builds have usage receipts. The local 27B game uses a different, shorter brief and is shown separately.
